wcag_20_a_description: Basic level of accessibility. Published in 2008.
wcag_20_a_recommendation: Outdated - recommended to upgrade to a newer version.
wcag_20_aa_description: Standard level of accessibility required by most legal regulations.
wcag_20_aa_recommendation: Outdated - recommended to upgrade to WCAG 2.1 AA or 2.2 AA.
wcag_20_aaa_description: Highest level of accessibility in WCAG 2.0.
wcag_21_a_description: Basic level with additional criteria for mobile devices and cognitive aspects.
wcag_21_a_recommendation: Good starting point, but AA level is recommended.
wcag_21_aa_description: Recommended standard for most websites. Adds 17 new criteria to WCAG 2.0.
wcag_21_aa_recommendation: Optimal choice for most projects - widely legally accepted.
wcag_21_aaa_description: Highest level of accessibility in WCAG 2.1.
wcag_21_aaa_recommendation: Excellent for critical services, but may be difficult to fully implement.
wcag_22_a_description: Latest basic level with additional cognitive criteria.
wcag_22_aa_description: Latest AA standard with 9 new success criteria published in October 2023.
wcag_22_aa_recommendation: Latest and best choice - future-proof legal standard.
wcag_22_aaa_description: Highest current level of accessibility with latest requirements.
wcag_22_aaa_recommendation: Ideal for organizations aiming for the highest accessibility.
group_exports_all: Exports include all findings and evidence, regardless of filters.
group_no_locator: No reliable element locator is available.
group_review_help: Select findings to group a confirmed shared problem. Enter your name and a reason for each decision. Page occurrences and original evidence are preserved.
group_combine_help: Combining requires the same issue type and outcome. Different issues on one element remain separate.
group_review_unverified_element: Possible match: element identity is unverified
group_review_possible_shared_problem: Possible shared problem across sampled pages
group_no_findings: No remediation findings were reported. Review the scope and any untested criteria before drawing conclusions.
group_not_conformance: These counts do not establish WCAG conformance.
group_report_note: Findings are grouped by specific problem. Occurrences and source observations are listed separately.
eval_intro: Choose representative pages and describe what each sample covers. Scan initial page states individually, then build a combined report.
eval_bulk_help: One complete URL per line. Query parameters, fragments and repeated URLs are preserved.
eval_bulk_error: Use valid HTTP or HTTPS URLs and keep the total at 20 samples or fewer. No rows were added.
eval_duplicate: This URL appears more than once. Keep both entries if they represent intentional samples or states.
eval_manual_help: This entry is retained in the sample set but cannot be scanned yet. State preparation will be added in a later stage.
eval_build_help: The combined report includes current scans only. Unscanned entries remain listed so missing coverage is visible.
eval_session_only: This draft and its scans are held in this tab. Export the combined report before closing or reloading.
eval_scan_coverage: Scanned samples: {scanned} of {total}. This does not indicate WCAG conformance.
eval_snapshot_help: This report captures the sample set at the time it was built. After editing samples or scanning again, build a new report.
